stops.title: Welcome to Isha Yoga Center
stops.about: Namaskaram! You are standing at the entrance of the Isha Yoga Center, a peaceful sanctuary nestled at the lush foothills of the Velliangiri Mountains in southern India. This sacred space was established by Sadhguru, a yogi and mystic who dedicated his life to sharing the ancient science of yoga with the modern world. According to Isha, this center serves as a powerful environment for your inner growth and wellbeing, offering paths of devotion, knowledge, action, and energy. People from every corner of the globe travel here to experience a deeper sense of fulfillment. Sadhguru describes his mission beautifully, saying, "This life for me is an endeavor to help people experience and express their divinity." As you walk through these grounds, you will find an international community of volunteers and residents living together in harmony. Whether you are here for a few hours or a longer stay, this space is open to everyone, inviting you to realize your full potential.

stops.title: Miracle of Mind
stops.about: Here is a little corner dedicated to Miracle of Mind. This is a completely free meditation application offered by Isha Foundation to support your daily clarity and peace. As the app puts it, "If your mind becomes a conscious process, it becomes the greatest miracle in existence." Rather than offering a crowded collection of choices, this app provides just one simple guided session that takes only seven minutes. You do not need any prior background in meditation, special physical flexibility, or particular beliefs to try it. According to Isha, if you can simply sit down safely and close your eyes, you can practice this quiet tool anywhere and at any time. It is designed to be a gentle technique for your wellbeing rather than a belief system to follow. Take a soft breath, explore the calm surrounding you, and remember that peacefulness can begin with just a few quiet moments every day.

stops.title: The Nandi
stops.about: Here at the entrance of the Dhyanalinga stands a magnificent figure: the Nandi. This impressive statue reaches fifteen feet in height, making it the largest of its kind in the world. As you look closer, you might notice its unique texture. According to Isha, it is crafted from metal and filled with a special mixture of sacred ash, herbs, and other ingredients that help it radiate a very specific energy. In Indian tradition, Nandi is not just a guardian; he represents a profound state of being. Isha describes the Nandi as a symbol of eternal waiting, the essential quality for receptivity. He is not waiting for something to happen; he is simply in a state of total stillness and alertness. By standing here with him, you are invited to leave behind your distractions. This quiet presence helps prepare your own system to be more open and receptive before you step inside the meditative space of the Dhyanalinga.

stops.title: The Dhyanalinga
stops.about: Now you are standing before the Dhyanalinga, a unique meditative space that welcomes everyone, regardless of their personal beliefs. The name carries a special meaning: in the ancient Sanskrit language, 'Dhyana' means meditation and 'Linga' means form. As you step inside the massive brick dome, you will notice there are no rituals or spoken prayers. Instead, the room is filled with a deep, powerful silence. According to Isha, this space was created to help every visitor find a sense of inner peace. To experience it, you can simply sit and gaze at the central form for a few moments. Then, close your eyes with your palms facing upward on your lap. Sadhguru says, 'Just sitting silently for a few minutes within the sphere of Dhyanalinga is enough to make even those unaware of meditation experience a state of deep meditativeness.' A bell rings every fifteen minutes to signal when to enter or leave. Please stay for at least one full cycle to enjoy the stillness.

stops.title: Linga Bhairavi
stops.about: This is the home of Linga Bhairavi. Look closely and you might notice her unique shape. Unlike traditional statues, she is manifested as a linga, representing the most exuberant expression of the divine feminine. According to Isha, she was consecrated by Sadhguru to support every aspect of your life, from your physical health to your inner success. You are in a space designed to feel like a nurturing mother's presence—both fierce and deeply compassionate. Sadhguru describes her as a powerful giver, saying, "Those who earn the Grace of Bhairavi neither have to live in concern or fear of life or death." As you walk through the temple, you can witness the daily offerings of fire and water, or simply sit quietly to soak in the vibrant energy. Whether you seek material prosperity or spiritual growth, this space is open to everyone. Feel the stability and grace here as you continue your journey through the center.

stops.title: Suryakund
stops.about:
This is the Suryakund. As you stand here, look down at the subterranean pool resting twenty feet below the ground level. Suspended above it is a magnificent sun sculpture crafted from brass and copper. According to Isha teachings, taking a dip in this vibrant pool is a traditional step to wet your entire body before stepping into sacred spaces like the Dhyanalinga.

This specific water body is consecrated with masculine energy and is reserved for male visitors, while women visit the nearby Chandrakund. Isha describes these energized waters as balancing and rejuvenating for both body and mind. Most importantly, it prepares your system to be far more receptive to the profound stillness waiting inside the main temple spaces. Take a moment to feel the peaceful atmosphere around this unique pool before you continue your journey.

stops.title: Chandrakund - Sacred Pool for Women
stops.about:
Chandrakund is a sacred energy pool created specifically for women visitors. As you step down toward these cool, peaceful waters, you are participating in a very ancient Indian tradition. According to Isha teachings, wetting your entire body before walking into a consecrated space gently opens your mind and system to receive deeper spiritual grace.

Bathing in this quiet subterranean pool offers much more than just a refreshing dip. Isha describes these energized waters as balancing and rejuvenating for both body and mind. Above all, stepping into Chandrakund serves as a gentle preparation for visiting the main Dhyanalinga dome. By allowing your energies to settle and align here, you become fully ready to experience the deep silence inside the temple space. Take your time, breathe deeply, and enjoy this serene moment of quiet preparation.

stops.title: Adiyogi and the Yogeshwara Linga
stops.about: Now look up at this magnificent steel face, you are standing before the world’s largest bust sculpture. According to Isha, this figure represents the very first yogi who shared the science of yoga with humanity over fifteen thousand years ago. He is a reminder of the human potential to rise above all limitations. The height of 112 feet is very special; it symbolizes the 112 different ways he offered for us to reach our highest nature. Sadhguru describes that "Adiyogi is the doorway to ultimate wellbeing and liberation." Just in front of him, you will find the Yogeshwara Linga. This sacred form was created to bring a living energy to this space. You might see people offering water or tying small black cloths nearby as a way to connect with this grace. Whether you choose to walk around him or sit quietly, may you feel the stillness of the mountains behind you.

stops.title: Save Soil Movement
stops.about: This stall is about the Conscious Planet movement. According to Isha, Save Soil is a global effort to protect the very foundation of our life. Sadhguru initiated this movement to bring people together and encourage leaders to pass laws that restore health to the earth. It is urgent: according to Save Soil, 52 percent of the world’s agricultural soils are already degraded. By increasing the organic matter in our fields, we can ensure that the food we grow is nutritious and the planet stays healthy for children everywhere. In short, Save Soil unites people across the globe to stand up for soil health. You can be a part of this change too. Whether it is writing a letter to a leader or simply learning more about the living earth, every small step helps. It is a gentle reminder that we are all connected to the soil, and together, we can make the world a greener, more vibrant home.

stops.title: Upa Yoga Hall
stops.about: This is the Upa Yoga Hall, a space dedicated to simple yet powerful tools for your wellbeing. Here, you can discover practices that fit easily into your daily life. According to Isha, Upa Yoga consists of pre-yoga exercises that activate your joints and muscles, bringing a sense of ease to your whole system. Isha explains that Upa Yoga means "sub-" or "pre-yoga": simple, useful processes with great benefits for body and mind. You may also learn Isha Kriya, a guided meditation designed to bring peace and dynamism. Isha explains that Kriya means an inward action, helping you connect with the source of your existence. For those seeking a deeper transformation, the Inner Engineering program offers tools to align your mind, body, and emotions. These practices are meant to help you establish a foundation of health and joy. Whether you are a beginner or have practiced before, these simple processes are here to help you create your life the way you want it.

stops.title: Bhiksha Hall and Annadanam
stops.about: Namaskaram. You are standing before the Bhiksha Hall, a space dedicated to the ancient tradition of Annadanam, or the sacred offering of food. According to Isha, providing nourishment to spiritual seekers has always been a vital part of this culture. As you step inside, you will notice a unique atmosphere of quiet focus. Here, two vegetarian meals are served every day to everyone at the center, from monks to visitors like yourself. Before eating, everyone joins in a powerful chant called an invocation. Sadhguru describes this as a way to make us more receptive to the life process. You are invited to eat in complete silence, turning the simple act of a meal into a conscious practice. By waiting for everyone to be served before starting, you build a sense of awareness and gratitude. Sadhguru says, "The most beautiful expression of this was the Annadhanam, the offering of food." This hall is more than a dining area; it is a place to nurture both your body and your inner growth.

stops.title: The Ancient Art of Kalaripayattu
stops.about: This is the ground for Kalaripayattu. As you stand here, you are stepping into a tradition that is thousands of years old. According to Isha, this is likely the most ancient martial art on Earth, passed down from the sage Agastya Muni. It is much more than just learning how to strike or defend yourself. Sadhguru describes it as a way of "learning to use the body in every possible way." You might see students practicing fluid movements, high kicks, or even training with wooden shields and flexible swords. This practice helps people understand their own energy and keeps the body in a healthy, regenerative state. For the students here, it is a spiritual journey and a more active form of yoga. It is truly wonderful to watch how they move with such grace, speed, and balance. As you observe, notice how every movement is designed to help the person explore the amazing possibilities of being human.

stops.title: The Gaushala and Bullock Carts
stops.about: The Gaushala is a peaceful sanctuary dedicated to protecting India’s native cattle. As you look around, you will see beautiful indigenous cows and strong bulls. According to Isha, these animals are vital to our heritage. Isha explains that in the yogic culture the cow is treated with great sanctity, because she is seen as a nourisher of life. This space was created to ensure these unique breeds continue to thrive. You might also notice the traditional bullock carts nearby. These are not just for show; they provide the bulls with meaningful activity that keeps them healthy and strong. To make sure the animals are comfortable, the carts use clever designs like smooth ball bearings and soft tires to keep the load very light. It is a wonderful way to experience a slower, traditional way of life. Whether you are watching the cows or taking a gentle ride, this place reminds us of the deep connection between humans and nature.

stops.title: Guru Pooja
stops.about: Good morning. As the sun begins to rise over the mountains, you are witnessing a beautiful ritual called Guru Pooja. According to Isha, this is much more than just a ceremony of thanks; it is a way to create a sacred space that invites the divine to be present. Sadhguru describes it as a process of making yourself 'choiceless,' meaning you give yourself so completely to the moment that the divine has no choice but to be with you. This tradition started long ago with the first yogi, Adiyogi, and his seven students. When they finished their learning, they offered everything back to him to show their devotion. Today, we still make sixteen symbolic offerings to remember that gesture of total emptiness. As you watch, try to be fully involved and inclusive in your heart. Sadhguru says, "Guru Pooja is not about offering a flower, a fruit, and a coconut – this is a subtle process to create an invitation to the Divine."

stops.title: Mahashivratri Celebrations
stops.about: Once a year, this space transforms into a vibrant sea of music and meditation on the darkest night of the year. According to Isha, this festival is not just a cultural event but a significant time for your physical and spiritual wellbeing. Isha explains that on this night the planetary positions create a natural upsurge of energy in the human body. To make the most of this, you are encouraged to stay awake and keep your spine in a vertical position through the whole night. As you look around, imagine the air filled with the sounds of ancient chants and the rhythm of world-class musicians. Isha calls it a unique opportunity to make use of the forces of nature for our wellbeing. Whether you are watching the dazzling light show on the Adiyogi statue or sitting in quiet reflection, this night offers a chance for deep inner growth. It is a time to celebrate the first teacher of yoga and the immense possibilities within every human being.
